## What's seed hacking? 

<br>

::: {.fragment .nobullet}
Manually adjusting features in your analysis to cause the random variation that is due purely to differences in random seeding to appear to demonstrate a non-random effect in line with your hypothesis
:::

::: {.fragment .arrow-fragment-before .fragment-index-3}
Selecting a\ *hyper*\ specific seed: 
:::


<!-- To make sure coin_flip is loaded in the later cell block's namespace -->

```{webr}  
#| envir: coin_flip
#| autorun: true
#| echo: false
coin_flip <- function(num_flips){
    flips = sample(x=c("H", "T"), size=num_flips, replace=TRUE)
    heads = sum(flips=="H")
    print(
        glue::glue(
            "Number of heads from {num_flips} coin flips: {heads}"
            )
        )
    return(invisible(heads))
}
```

## What if  [gasp]{style="text-decoration:underline solid"} no seed!?

::: {.fragment}
How R handles this: generate a *random* random seed at the time you first need it
:::

::: {.fragment}
maybe something here about set.seed(NULL) and then later abotu shimming it
:::

::: {.fragment}
Benefit: not known beforehand...
:::

::: {.fragment}
Drawback: not reproducible...
:::

::: {.fragment .subbullet .indent_}
Also, who's to say you didn't set your seed in your environment beforehand?
:::

## new: even more scary: what if set.seed() gets shimmed in the console before executing?

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
#| echo: false 
#| envir: shim_set_seed

set.seed <- function(i) {base::set.seed(614)}
```

```{webr}
#| envir: shim_set_seed
# Set in the console beforehand:
# > set.seed <- function(i){base::set.seed(614)}

# Flip 10 coins
sample(c("H","T"), size=10, replace=TRUE)
```

::: {.fragment}
'It works on my machine...'
:::

::: {.fragment}
Some solutions:
:::

- docker (ship the machine)...but still can run the shim in the console
    - not everyone has docker/can fit heavy containers/learning is a pain/intimidating
- public, remote execution 

<!-- ------------------------------------------ SLIDE BREAK -->
solution: keep code the same: base::set.seed(beacr::get_seed(...)), use one seed for development/pilot testing (or as many as you wish; you can change often; defaults to using the same for ease of use) and then when time to deploy (after data collection finished, after a given date, at a certain pulse index...i kinda need help deciding how best to do this, but ghactions can facilitate any. The point is that you commit during the prereg to a timepoint so that if you do or may have access to the data beforehand you can't just keep running it every minute until you get a seed from the beacon that you like.

gh action
`RUN rm beacr/seed_log.json`
`RUN 

```yaml
jobs:
    run_with_fresh-seed:
        steps:
            name: purge seed used for development
            run: rm beacr/seed_log.json # bash
            # OR 
            run: Rscript -e "beacr::reset_seed_log(purge_all=TRUE, yes_to_all=TRUE)"

            name: run 
            # targets::tar_make() (CONFIRM THIS IS HOW)
            # rmarkdown::render("analysis.Rmd")
            #

            name: publish results for transparency

```

- drawbacks: what if publishign step fails? 
- is this log public? can the history be spoofed or tampered with?
- is there a solution that is decentralized//doesn't make us rely on github? ehh kinda need some computing infrastructure; someone has to pay for the machines


*more on that ... later...
<!-- ------------------------------------------ SLIDE BREAK -->
So now we're at a place where we have maybe a solution to the issue of "how to run it so that you can accurately record the seed used" but HOW DO YOU CHOOSE A SEED? 

Qualities:
- has to be unknown before 1) hypothesis is published (prereg) and ideally 2) data collection has finished 
-   - why after data collection finished?: no ordering effects 9


Some ideas how: 
- precommit to a date (or a number of dates for backup), or after N participants' data have been collected, etc: something that precludes collecting more data after the seed is known 
- central repository/hub that handles the entire project (hub and spoke model; osf for registration, xyz for data store, etc); ggithub action to wait for a fresh pulse (e.g. not just 60s bc may be some error in the beacon but until a literal new pulse) and then use that new pulse as the seed for the analysis, 
    - added benefit of on-demand running: can continue to validate/audit as more data is collected (running public tally) 
    - interesting thing about github; can you make it so ppl can run actions but the results of their runs aren't comitted if they aren't maintainers//can be verified by reviewers?
